conclusion: No blocking findings. The independently reviewed statepair executor keeps the frozen numerical and evaluation gates, merges both training and token inventories, and isolates new probe/main artifacts from the historical preauth reference.
reviewed_invariants: Execution rows equal the frozen old pool plus additions; the full statepair schedule is validated before model training.
Actual prompt encoding and cached tokens are checked against the merged old and candidate token lengths; re-signed same-length cache tampering is rejected.
Probe and main use separate statepair results, controls, caches and checkpoint paths; the historical reference uses preauth step 400.
Fresh official same-seed initialization is compared with archived preauth and successful probe initial trainable tensor hashes.
A 25-step train-only probe uses the original 400-step learning rate and must pause at step 12, restore in a new process, then execute step 13.
Main requires a successful bound probe with an exited worker; probe adapters cannot initialize main.
Shared GPU lock and launch guard prevent duplicate execution; pause waits for original PID and creation-time identity to exit and confirms checkpoint integrity and lock release.
Only statepair step 400 is eligible for selection; step 200 is diagnostic and historical preauth is a comparison only.
Calibration and final evaluation remain gated behind the original development and calibration criteria; the probe rejects all evaluation splits.
CPU candidate and schedule training-disabled metadata remain immutable; the separately authorized execution protocol records training permission.
limitations: This is source review and synthetic CPU verification, not proof of successful GPU training or pause/resume on the real worker.
No model weights, evaluation examples or historical predictions were loaded by this reviewer.
The numerical/runtime/model-reference preflight reported by the parent was not independently rerun by this reviewer.
